text:
NICE NG51 covers the recognition, diagnosis and early management of suspected sepsis in all age groups, in hospital and community settings. It was first published in 2016 and updated in 2024, and remains the current UK national guideline for sepsis.

RECOGNITION AND RISK STRATIFICATION: Assess people with suspected infection using structured clinical assessment plus the NEWS2 score, which combines respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, systolic blood pressure, pulse rate and level of consciousness. Stratify into high risk, moderate-to-high risk, or low risk of severe illness or death from sepsis using age-specific criteria covering behaviour and mental status, heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, capillary refill, urine output, skin appearance (mottled, ashen, cyanosed, non-blanching rash) and temperature.

HIGH-RISK PATIENTS: Take blood cultures before giving antibiotics where this does not delay treatment. Measure venous blood gas including lactate and glucose, full blood count, C-reactive protein, urea and electrolytes, creatinine, liver function tests and a clotting screen. Give a broad-spectrum antibiotic within 1 hour of recognizing high risk, following local antimicrobial guidance. Give intravenous fluid resuscitation to patients with signs of shock. Arrange urgent review by a senior clinical decision-maker and consider critical-care referral.

MODERATE-TO-HIGH RISK: Arrange clinician review within 1 hour of meeting a single moderate-to-high-risk criterion. Where no definitive alternative diagnosis is found and lactate is below 2 mmol/litre with no acute kidney injury, repeat structured assessment at least hourly and ensure a senior clinical decision-maker reviews the need for antibiotics within 3 hours.

ONGOING CARE: Identify and treat the source of infection (source control). Reassess response to fluids and antibiotics; escalate to critical care if there is no improvement. Give written and verbal information to patients and carers about what sepsis is, which symptoms to monitor after discharge, and when to seek urgent help. The guideline also sets out training requirements so that all staff who may encounter sepsis can recognize it early.
title: NICE NG51 — Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
